clue.text: Coaches county seconds

definitions.note: plural noun: horse-drawn carriages, matching the plural answer

parts.note: Surrey is an English county just south-west of London
s is the standard abbreviation for seconds of time

explanation.surface: Sports coaches from one county take second place, or a county's coaches ferry its second team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaches' reads as trainers or buses, but here it means light four-wheeled carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: A surrey is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, so several of them are coaches in the old sense.

clue.text: Feature of room provided uplifting change

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: provided means if, as in 'provided it rains'
to change something is to replace it

explanation.surface: Something in a room, offered as a cheering update to the decor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' looks like praise of the change, but in this down clue it turns IF upwards into FI.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearth set into a wall is a classic focal point in a sitting room.

clue.text: Scan the melody in part song

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A music student is told to scan a melody that forms part of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A rousing hymn or national tune sung by a crowd is a kind of song.

clue.text: I boast highbrow subject introduced by appropriate presenter

definitions.note: the words a show-off might say about himself, standing for the person

indicators.note: introduced by means the subject comes after the presenter's name

parts.note: Melvyn Bragg presented The South Bank Show, a British arts programme, so he is fitting for an arts subject
art is a cultured, highbrow subject

explanation.surface: A cultured topic is fronted by a well-chosen television host.
explanation.walkthrough: Melvyn Bragg is a British broadcaster famous for the arts series The South Bank Show, hence 'appropriate' for art.
explanation.definitionFit: A boaster is someone forever saying 'I boast', so the clue's quotation stands for the person who says it.

clue.text: Crazy golf place — club to go wrong at the start

definitions.note: the answer is an idiom used as an adjective, so it fits 'crazy'

indicators.note: at the start places the club and the wrongdoing before the golf venue

parts.note: a bat is a club used to hit a ball
to sin is to do wrong
The Belfry is a famous golf course in the English Midlands that has hosted the Ryder Cup

explanation.surface: A crazy golf course where a club misbehaves on the first hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy golf' reads as one phrase, but 'Crazy' is the definition and 'golf place' gives THE BELFRY, a Midlands course that has hosted the Ryder Cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Having bats in the belfry is an idiom for being eccentric or mad.

clue.text: Star in danger taking two separate directions

indicators.note: taking means the phrase takes letters into itself
separate says the two compass points go in at different spots, not side by side

parts.note: to be in danger is to be at risk
E is east, one compass direction
S is south, the other compass direction

explanation.surface: A celebrity in peril heads off two different ways at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separate' says the two compass points go in at different places: S after the A and E after the T of AT RISK.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed symbol * is shaped like a star and is often called a star.

clue.text: Good landlord provides spirit

parts.note: a pub landlord is the host of the house

explanation.surface: A decent pub landlord serves up spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like the drink a landlord sells, but it is the definition: a phantom.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom of the dead is commonly called a spirit.

clue.text: Thief is person in charge around street

indicators.note: around means the ruler goes round the street

parts.note: a ruler is a person in charge

explanation.surface: A burglar turns out to be the local boss living round the corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler steals cattle or horses, a particular kind of thief.

clue.text: Bishop's joint a job for chiropodist

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a union is a joint where two things are joined

explanation.surface: A churchman's sore joint needs a foot specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: A chiropodist is a foot doctor (a podiatrist).
explanation.definitionFit: A painful swelling on the big toe is a typical case for a foot doctor to treat.

clue.text: A bird's exciting times out

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A girlfriend enjoys thrilling nights out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is British slang for a young woman, which makes the surface read as gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tit is a small songbird, and this is an old name for one.

clue.text: What riders wear jumping Becher's, consuming energy

indicators.note: consuming means the rearranged letters swallow another
jumping suits horses going over a fence, and signals the name's letters leap into a new order

parts.note: Becher's Brook, a fence at the Grand National steeplechase in Britain
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Jockeys' clothing as they clear Becher's Brook, using up their stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping' rearranges BECHERS into BRECHES, and 'consuming' puts E inside it. Becher's Brook is a famous fence at the Grand National, Britain's biggest steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding breeches are the short trousers fastened below the knee worn on horseback.

clue.text: Conductor's upset

definitions.meaning: Sir Simon ..., the British orchestral conductor

explanation.surface: An orchestra leader is put out.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Rattle is a famous conductor, and to fluster someone is to put them off balance.

clue.text: Cancel my orders for plant

indicators.note: orders as a verb means puts in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone calls off their flower orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' reads as purchases in the surface but is the verb 'arranges'.
explanation.definitionFit: A low flowering perennial with swept-back petals, grown as a houseplant.

clue.text: Record of top cricket match that was once broadcast in quiet periods

definitions.text: that was once broadcast in quiet periods

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match, the highest level
a scorecard is the record of a cricket match

explanation.surface: The scorecard of a big cricket match was aired during lulls.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is international cricket's top fixture; the 'of' places the record after the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Television channels showed a still image, famously a girl with a clown, when no programmes were scheduled.

clue.text: Minor leader — one participating in revolutionary affair

indicators.note: participating in means the numeral takes a place inside the following words

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's standard revolutionary
I is the Roman numeral for one
a fling is a brief affair

explanation.surface: A junior leader becomes part of a revolutionary romance.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ling makes a diminutive, so this is a petty or lesser chief.

clue.text: US lawman to make point — it helps to listen

parts.note: Wyatt Earp, the Wild West marshal
to hone a blade is to sharpen it to a point

explanation.surface: An American sheriff makes his point, which helps others to hear him.
explanation.definitionFit: A small speaker worn at the ear is a device that aids listening.

clue.text: Deny being negative in a fit of temper

indicators.note: in means the negative goes inside the following words

parts.note: bate is British informal for a rage, as in 'in a bate'

explanation.surface: Refusing to be pessimistic while in a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: BATE is old-fashioned British slang for a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To abnegate is to renounce or refuse oneself something, a formal synonym of deny.

clue.text: Second-rate celebrity is a pest

definitions.meaning: a B-list celebrity is one of the second rank of fame
an annoying person, an informal sense of a skin bubble

explanation.surface: A minor celebrity is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A B-list star is a second-rate celebrity; informally a tiresome person is also called a blister.

clue.text: One used to pray for fool in debt

indicators.note: in means the fool goes inside the word for debt

parts.note: hock as in 'in hock', owing money or pawned
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A worshipper prays for an idiot who owes money.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick cushion for kneeling on in church is used during prayer.

clue.text: British manager sacked — he gets lighter work

indicators.note: sacked means wrecked or ransacked, so the letters of the word are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A British football manager is fired and finds an easier job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter' looks like 'less heavy' but is a flat-bottomed boat for moving cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a cargo boat, so its crewman gets work on a lighter.

clue.text: One who's beaten up needs start of emergency repair at last

indicators.note: at last puts that first letter at the end
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a loser is one who has been beaten

indicators.note: start of means take the first letter of the word emergency

explanation.surface: A beaten-up victim needs emergency treatment in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten up' reads as a phrase, but 'up' alone reverses LOSER to RESOL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To resole shoes is to repair them by fitting new soles.

clue.text: Boost for royal consort proclaimed

indicators.note: proclaimed means said out loud, so the answer sounds like the name

parts.note: Prince Philip, the husband of Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A boost for the Queen's husband is announced.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or encouragement that lifts something.

clue.text: Gave false report about North having rules

indicators.note: about means the lie goes around the letter

parts.note: to give a false report is to lie

explanation.surface: Someone misreported a northern area's regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rules' reads as regulations, but means ruled lines, as on writing paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing paper with ruled lines printed on it is described as lined.

clue.text: Stay more upright, lacking interest

definitions.meaning: to list is to lean, so leaning less means staying more upright
apathetic and without energy or enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Advice to stand up straight, given to someone bored.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the answer splits as LIST LESS: lean over less, as a ship that lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone apathetic and without enthusiasm is said to be languid and bored.

clue.text: Stick around northern party to see rugby player

indicators.note: around means the stick goes round the other letters

parts.note: a staff is a walking stick
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone with a stick hangs around a northern party to watch a rugby star.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the fly-half position is also called by this name.

clue.text: Peacekeepers in intricate act of madness

indicators.note: in means the peacekeepers go inside the other word

parts.note: lacy means intricate like lace
the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping forces caught up in a complicated insane act.
explanation.definitionFit: A foolish or crazy deed can be called a lunacy, a piece of insanity.

clue.text: Dickens character in uninteresting, dull work

indicators.note: in means the character goes inside the other word

parts.note: dry means dull and uninteresting
Barnaby Rudge, the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A Dickens character trapped in tedious, dreary toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Drudgery is hard, menial and monotonous labour.
